$Comment: The Master wage: what a woodcutter at the top of Trim Work earns for one order, once luck
decides how the run actually went. Mmo_Sawmill_Trim_Pay routes here on level alone; everything
below reads the woodcutter's own Woodcutting luck and the global luck channel at equal weight
(this is the mill's own trade, so Crafting luck is left out), so within this tier a lucky run
pays noticeably more than an unlucky one even though both workers stand at the same point in
UNITS, the one trap worth knowing. MMO_Luck_WOODCUTTING and MMO_Luck both store WHOLE-NUMBER
percent readings, not fractions: a fully claimed Woodcutting tree, the trophy hatchet in hand
and the woodcutter's kit worn together read somewhere near a hundred and sixty-six on the
station's own channel, which is what the top floor here is sized against; MMO_Luck ships empty
by default, so a server or pack that grants global luck is respected here without moving that
ceiling. Never swap either for the mmoskilltree:station_luck aggregate: that one returns a
FRACTION and would shift every floor by a factor of a hundred.
RANGES pay experience and essence drawn evenly between Amount/Count and their Max, decided once
per claim, which is what keeps two runs at the same floor from reading identically.
PULLS. Each floor's DropLists array names MMO_Station_Trim_Offcuts_T4 once per pull; listing the
same id twice rolls it twice, independently, so the count of entries IS the number of pulls.
THE TOP FLOOR CARRIES A CUE. It wants a maxed level AND a heavily invested luck tree at once, so
it is genuinely occasional and earns the celebration; every floor below it stays silent.
Name: Mmo_Sawmill_Trim_Wage_Master

Rolls.$Comment: Luck alone decides the floor. Retune a number here without touching the level router.
